items.title: A solo coder used Claude Code to build a Wi-Fi jam detector
items.why: An ESP32-C5 touchscreen board learns the RF baseline then flags jamming on 2.4/5GHz - open source, build your own this weekend.

items.title: A 149M local model handles 70% of phone-agent steps, Claude the rest
items.why: Confident steps stay on a cheap on-device model; hard ones route to Claude - matches Claude alone at under a third the cost.

items.title: Box breathing before a mock job interview measurably cut stress markers
items.why: A 5-min box-breathing session before a simulated hiring interview lowered heart rate and stress-hormone spikes versus normal breathing.

items.title: Heavy-light decomposition: the chain trick for fast tree path queries
items.why: Splits a tree into O(log n) chains so any path query becomes a few segment-tree lookups - a real differentiator in interviews and CF.

items.title: A full 386 PC emulator is being ported to run on a $1 RP2350 chip
items.why: Tiny386, which already boots DOS and lean Linux on an ESP32, is being adapted for the RP2350 - a weekend retro-PC build on cheap hardware.

items.title: Mice replay practiced skills in sleep even with their memory hub disabled
items.why: Procedural-memory replay ran fine without the hippocampus in mice - early, mouse-only evidence, not yet confirmed in humans.
items.source: Nature Neuroscience (Thompson, Rollik et al., UCL)

items.title: Someone bolted Monte Carlo tree search onto Claude Code
items.why: Open-source attempt to make Claude branch and backtrack like a game-tree search instead of one linear attempt - debated, but forkable.

items.title: 90-120 minutes of weekly strength training looks like the sweet spot
items.why: A 150,000-person, 3-decade cohort found mortality benefits plateaued past 2 hours/week of lifting - more wasn't better, consistency was.
items.source: British Journal of Sports Medicine (Harvard Chan School)

items.title: Linux is adding a tool whose only job is to crash your kernel on purpose
items.why: hwpoison-panic injects a fake memory-failure error to verify panic-on-failure settings actually work - handy for testing your own setup.

items.title: AI's data glut is quietly reviving magnetic tape storage
items.why: Cloud operators use offline tape vaults as a cheap, ransomware-proof place to dump AI-era data - old tech solving a new-scale problem.
